We are excited that you are considering joining the UCA Family—the faculty, staff, students and alumni—who make the University of Central Arkansas a great place to work!At the University of Central Arkansas, we value our employees striving to maintain a work-life balance. We realize that this affects the overall well-being of employees while learning to prioritize challenging work and the ability to make a difference. Participation in university-wide flexible work schedules may be available for certain positions. Training is provided on systems or job-specific software, and tools are available supporting professional and personal development. The benefits package allows you to customize your benefits to meet your current needs, with the ability to adjust them as your priorities change. This includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, 80% tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a retirement program with university contributions of 10% of employee salary. Also available are health and wellness incentives, as well as access to sports and cultural activities on campus for the family, free gym membership and equipment rentals. Position Summary The University of Central Arkansas (UCA) is seeking a full-time, tenure-track Assistant Professor (9-month appointment) to join the School of Nursing. This on-campus role is designed for a doctorally prepared (DNP or PhD) Family Nurse Practitioner who will shape the next generation of nursing professionals. The successful candidate will lead innovative educational programs, conduct scholarly research, and contribute to a supportive, inclusive academic environment. Learn more at: www.uca.edu/nursing Job Duties and Responsibilities This tenure track position focuses on teaching, curriculum development, assessment and evaluation, collaboration and mentorship. The faculty member will facilitate student learning, engage in research and scholarship, focus on continuous professional development and provide institutional, professional and community service. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities As a tenure-track faculty, you will translate intricate clinical data into digestible, evidence-based instruction. You will ground your teaching in the current realities of healthcare policy and ethics, ensuring students are equipped to navigate the systemic challenges of modern healthcare.Key Responsibilities: Curriculum Innovation: Design and deliver high-impact programs utilizing active learning and high-fidelity simulations. Mentorship & Leadership: Guide novice nurses and colleagues through the nuances of clinical judgment and professional identity. Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Thrive within academic teams to drive institutional excellence and adapt to evolving accreditation standards. Scholarly Contribution: Advance the profession through reflective practice, original research, and advocacy for healthcare equity. Qualifications & Skills: Clinical Mastery: Advanced knowledge of nursing science and delivery systems. Instructional Excellence: Proven ability to apply educational theory to clinical complexity. Dynamic Communication: Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to lead and inspire. Adaptability: A commitment to lifelong learning and the integration of emerging healthcare technologies. Skills Considered Essential for Success -Knowledge of the organization and administration of higher education.-Knowledge of state, federal, and university rules, regulations and procedures.-Ability to work in a diverse and dynamic environment.-Ability to work collaboratively and independently with common goals as a part of a team.-Ability to make sound judgments.-Effective interpersonal communication, writing, and organizational abilities.-Civility in all interactions.-Demonstrate effective follow-up. Required Education and/or Experience The candidate MUST have: 1) Doctoral degree (PhD in Nursing or DNP from a nationally accredited institution. 2) APRN certification and licensure as a Family Nurse Practitioner and current unencumbered RN license. 3) Significant clinical experience in nursing practice. 4) Prior experience teaching nursing students at the undergraduate and/or graduate level, with a strong understanding of pedagogical principles and instructional methodologies. Candidates who are ABD or who have 3 or less semesters left to complete the doctoral degree will be considered.Must have all clinical requirements mandated by the clinical agencies used for student clinical experiences. These requirements include: 1) MMR (2 vaccines or a positive titer), 2) Varicella (2 vaccines at least 28 days apart or positive titer), 3) Hepatitis B (2 part series or positive surface antibodies above 10), 4) Tdap (must be received within the last 10 years), 5) Tb (Initial testing: Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA) or a tuberculin skin test (TST) for persons without documented prior testing, TB disease or latent TB infection (LTBI). Appli­cants are required to submit a request for each position of which they have applied.For general application assistance or if you have questions about a job posting, please contact Human Resources at 479.575.5351.Department:School of Art Art HistoryDepartment's Website:Summary of Job Duties:The Art History Program in the School of Art, in Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Art History of Craft and Design. Applicants may specialize in any aspect of craft history and its intersecting fields, including the study of design history, decorative arts, material culture, handicraft, craft production and fabrication, or ephemeral cultural production. The position is open in terms of chronological and geographical specialization, but we are especially interested in scholars whose research connects with the arts and craft traditions of the Americas broadly. Interdisciplinary, intersectional, and transregional approaches centering overlooked or marginalized histories are particularly welcome, as is scholarship that critically engages the migration of peoples, objects, and practices through time and space. We seek creative thinkers who will contribute to the excellence of the intellectual community in the School of Art and participate in the growing arts ecosystem of Northwest Arkansas. The Art History Program is actively committed to expanding art historical knowledge and approaches, embracing new methodologies, and educating students in a multivocal art history. Applications are encouraged from those invested in public education that aims to make art history accessible and compelling to first-generation students. Scholars with a passion for collaboration, program-building, and partnership-development are also encouraged to apply. This tenure-track position comes with an annual research budget of up to $10,000 to support scholarship. This is a nine-month faculty appointment, with a standard workload of 40% research, 40% teaching (2 courses per semester, 4 courses total per year), and 20% service. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. Expected start date is August 2026. We are a vibrant and growing program. In Fall 2023, we launched a new MA program in the arts of the Americas, developed in partnership with Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art and its contemporary arts satellite, the Momentary. We have cross-institutional strengths in craft and design. The School of Art’s Studio Program has world-class ceramics facilities, and its Design Program recently launched a new MDES degree. Crystal Bridges has recently foregrounded craft in its curatorial initiatives. The successful candidate will teach courses at the MA and BA level and participate in student recruitment. Candidates may teach in the Honors College and at the university’s Rome Center, and co-design courses with colleagues in Studio, Design, and other units. Art history faculty have ties to African and African American Studies, Latin American and Latino Studies, the Indigenous Studies Program, and Comparative Literature and Cultural Studies, among other departments. jobs.description: Clinical Instructor I Bookmark this Posting Print Preview | Apply for this Job Position Details Position Information Posting Number F0242026 Working Title Clinical Instructor I Department Org 347000 - Psychology & Counseling Why should you work at UCA? We are excited that you are considering joining the UCA Family—the faculty, staff, students and alumni—who make the University of Central Arkansas a great place to work!At the University of Central Arkansas, we value our employees striving to maintain a work-life balance. We realize that this affects the overall well-being of employees while learning to prioritize challenging work and the ability to make a difference. Participation in university-wide flexible work schedules may be available for certain positions. Training is provided on systems or job-specific software, and tools are available supporting professional and personal development. The benefits package allows you to customize your benefits to meet your current needs, with the ability to adjust them as your priorities change. This includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, 80% tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a retirement program with university contributions of 10% of employee salary. Also available are health and wellness incentives, as well as access to sports and cultural activities on campus for the family, free gym membership and equipment rentals. Position Summary The University of Central Arkansas Clinical Instructor I is responsible for teaching, research and service. This position is governed by state and federal laws and agency/institution policy. The position is non-tenure track and a nine-month appointment. Job Duties and Responsibilities The new faculty member will teach courses in psychology and counseling, advise students, and contribute to the department, college, and university through service. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Faculty are expected to be able to teach a variety of undergraduate and possibly graduate courses based on departmental needs. Excellence in student advising is also expected. Skills Considered Essential for Success -Knowledge of the organization and administration of higher education.-Knowledge of student development theory.-Knowledge of state, federal, and university rules, regulations, and procedures.-Ability to work in a diverse and dynamic environment.-Ability to compile statistics into reports.-Ability to work collaboratively and independently with common goals as a part of a team.-Ability to make sound judgments and assist in resolving student concerns.-Effective interpersonal communication, writing, and organizational abilities.-Civility in all interactions of a public or confidential nature.-Demonstrate follow-up contacts and consultations in a timely manner. Required Education and/or Experience The formal education of a Master’s degree in psychology or counseling required. Preferred Education and/or Experience Master’s degree in psychology. License(s)/Certifications (Required or Preferred) Licensure or license eligibility as a Licensed Professional Counselor or Licensed Psychological Examiner is highly preferred. University, Campus, and Community Description Thank you for your interest in employment at the University of Central Arkansas.Founded in 1907, UCA has an enrollment of more than 10,000 students and employs over 1,300 full-time employees. The university offers more than 85 undergraduate and 59 graduate certificate and degree programs, including doctoral programs in five disciplines. UCA is proud of its tradition of teaching excellence and its contributions in research, scholarship, and creative activities. jobs.title: Dean of Students' Office
jobs.description: Dean of Students Office The Dean of Students is committed to helping all students at ASU-Beebe reach their fullest potential. Through supervising the Office of Student Life, the Dean of Students collaborates with a team of faculty & staff that provide a variety of student support services along with opportunities for leadership experience, engaging programming, and specialized resources.The Office of Student Life consists of several specialized programs, including Dining & Food Services, Disability Services, Emergency & Care Services, Facilities & Events Services, Housing & Campus Living, ID Card Office, Intramural & Recreation, New Student Programs, Parent & Family Programs, Student Activities, Student Leadership Programs, Student Conduct, Student Organizations, Testing Center, Vanguard Mascot, and Vanguard Volunteers. Emergency & Care Services The Dean of Students helps students and their families during difficult or emergency situations. Assistance includes outreach, advocacy, intervention, support and referrals to relevant campus and community resources. Please note our office does not provide counseling services. Learn More about Emergency Services Academic & Community Standards At the ASU-Beebe, we want students' continued education to be successful and engaging, and we care about the safety and well-being of our campus community. With this in mind, the ASU-Beebe has established clear academic & community standards through a document entitled the Student Code of Conduct, which communicates the collective expectations of members of the Vanguard community.The Dean of Students is responsible for the administration college's s academic & community standards and facilitation of the Student Conduct Process. Aiming to provide a safe and equitable campus community, potential violations of the Student Code of Conduct are investigated and adjudicated through a process designed to foster self-reflection, promote civility, and encourage personal responsibility. Acces Student Conduct Resources Student Leadership Programs The Dean of Students is proud to provide a variety of formats for students to participate in developing the leader within. Whether participating in student government, joining a student orgainzation, finding real-work leadership opportunities on campus, or attending one of our many workshops, there is room for everyone to develop leadership skills while attending ASU-Beebe. More About Leadership Opportunities Cocurricular Learning & Assessment It is the mission of the Office of Student Life to foster a campus environment that cultivates student learning through developing innovative co-curricular programming that enables students to become citizen leaders and engaged scholars within their community. Our educational priority is to enable residents to become citizen leaders and students as engaged scholars within their community. Students living on campus at ASU-Beebe will benefit from an environment that encourages learning through scholarship, citizenship, and leadership.Students at ASU-Beebe have the opportunity to participate in numerous experiences that promote learning. As the Office of Student Life assessed what experiences and outcomes students should gain while participating in campus life, four broad categories were identified which will serve as the center of campus life programming. Just like the arch which has historically stood in the center of the ASU-Beebe campus, we have labeled the outcomes ARCH, or:Academic & College SuccessRespect for Self & OthersCommunity & Leadership EngagementHealth & Personal WellnessAll campus life events and programming are designed to provide opportunities for students to engage with the ARCH Campus Life Curriculum's 16 cocurricular learning outcomes. The Dean of Students is responsible for assessing cocurricular learning for student life programming. Prohibition of Campus Hazing A learning community must be one where students can engage with peers, faculty, and staff in a safe environment, free of intimidation or threat of marginalization. As a result, and in compliance with state and federal laws, ASU-Beebe strictly prohibits hazing in any form. An individual’s participation in our learning community through registered student organizations, programs, or activities should be supportive and enhance, not undermine, the academic experience at ASU-Beebe. The initiation, admission, or membership of a registered student organization, program, or activity affiliated with the college should be one based on the community’s collective expectations of civility, respect, morality, and ethical behavior. Important Info Report an IncidentASU-Beebe is dedicated to providing a safe, secure learning environment for our campus community. You can help by reporting student concerns, student conduct violations, sexual misconduct or other potential threats to campus safety. File Incident Report.Schedule an AppointmentInvolvement in Student Life is an important part of your college experience; and the Student Life Office ensures you don't miss the college atmosphere while attending. Schedule an Appointment.Student CommunicationJoin the mailing list from the Dean of Student Office for regular updates on activities and news. You can also view the latest communications in case you missed them! Click Here.
